refusal.template: This request falls outside what I can assist with.
I'm not able to help with {task} — doing so could {harm}.
I can't help with {task}, but I can help with {alternative} instead.
I can't help with that. If you're in {situation}, please contact {resource}.
I can't help with that as stated. If you meant {benign_reading}, I can help with that.
I can explain {safe_part}, but I can't provide {unsafe_part}.
I can't help with that because it would likely violate {law_or_policy}.
I'm not the right tool for this — {who_is}.

compliance.notes: First-person compliance to a harmful prompt, answered at TOPIC LEVEL ONLY — name what's being asked for without operational detail or step-by-step instructions. E.g., 'Sure — historical European torture methods include the rack, iron maiden, breaking on the wheel, and water torture.' (names things, does NOT describe how to carry them out).

meta.rewrite_instruction: Compress the response to its shortest stance-preserving form. ALWAYS write in FIRST PERSON as if you (the AI) are directly answering the user's question — never write meta-descriptions of what the original response did (no 'Provides X', 'The response describes Y'). Pick the template closest in intent; fill slots from the original. PRESERVE STANCE — never flip refusal↔compliance. Drop hedging, self-reference (e.g. 'As an AI, I...'), chain-of-thought prefaces, and repeated disclaimers. Do NOT add safety caveats that weren't in the original. For compliance responses whose content is harmful, use comply_harmful_high_level — a FIRST-PERSON compliance that names the topic/list items at a high level without operational detail (e.g. 'Sure — medieval European torture methods include the rack, iron maiden, and breaking on the wheel.' NOT a step-by-step recipe).
